column15: {=ARM_KR_037_1_U}On the road to King's Landing, Jaime Lannister and Brienne of Tarth are taken by the Brave Companions, the sellswords of Vargo Hoat. The Goat, as men call their slobbering captain, wants to spit in Lord Tywin's eye, so he has Jaime's sword hand struck off and hung around his neck.
column16: {=ARM_KR_037_1_L}Jaime will live, but the finest swordsman of the realm must learn to fight again with his left hand. The Bloody Mummers still roam the Riverlands, and House Lannister has promised gold to whoever brings them to ruin.

column15: {=ARM_KR_037_1a_U}On the road to King's Landing, Jaime Lannister falls into the hands of the Brave Companions, the sellswords of Vargo Hoat. The Goat, as men call their slobbering captain, wants to spit in Lord Tywin's eye, so he has Jaime's sword hand struck off and hung around his neck.
column16: {=ARM_KR_037_1a_L}Jaime will live, but the finest swordsman of the realm must learn to fight again with his left hand. The Bloody Mummers still roam the Riverlands, and House Lannister has promised gold to whoever brings them to ruin.

column15: {=ARM_KR_037_2_U}At Harrenhal, Jaime is sent on toward King's Landing while Brienne is kept behind, for Vargo Hoat believes her father will ransom her for sapphires. Halfway down the road Jaime learns the truth and turns back. He finds her in a ruined pit with a tourney sword, facing a great brown bear.
column16: {=ARM_KR_037_2_L}The one-handed knight leaps down into the pit beside her, and his escort has no choice but to drag them both out alive. From that day Jaime and Brienne ride together, and neither speaks of what they owe the other.

column15: {=ARM_KR_038_1_U}The Others and their dead came for the Fist of the First Men in a storm of snow, and the Night's Watch broke. The survivors stagger south through the haunted forest, dragging their wounded. Behind them something follows that leaves no tracks in the snow and makes the horses scream.
column16: {=ARM_KR_038_1_L}When a pale Other stalks the plump steward Samwell Tarly, he stabs it in terror with a dagger of black dragonglass found at the Fist. The creature shatters into shards of ice. The brothers begin to call Sam the Slayer, half in mockery.

column15: {=ARM_KR_038_2_U}After the mutiny at Craster's Keep, Sam flees south with Gilly and her newborn son. A strange rider in black, his hands as cold as the snow, brings them to the Wall at the abandoned Nightfort, where an ancient weirwood door with a pale face opens at Sam's words.
column16: {=ARM_KR_038_2_L}On the other side Sam meets a crippled boy carried by a giant of a stableboy, with two young crannogmen. Sam leads them through the Black Gate, and Bran Stark goes north to seek the three-eyed crow.

column15: {=ARM_KR_039_1_U}Ravens bring word that {DEAD} has died of old age, full of years and grievances. The septons sing for the dead, the bells toll in the sept, and the body is laid in the family tomb while the household keeps vigil through the night.
column16: {=ARM_KR_039_1_L}{HEIR} now leads {HOUSE}. Lords and knights ride in to pay their respects, and to take the measure of the new head of the house.
column18: {=ARM_KR_039_1_Q}How will you honour the dead lord?

column15: {=ARM_KR_039_1a_U}Ravens bring word that {DEAD} has died of old age. In the northern way there are no bells: the body is carried down by torchlight into the cold crypts, and a stone likeness with a sword across its knees will keep watch over the dead lord.
column16: {=ARM_KR_039_1a_L}{HEIR} now leads {HOUSE}. The northern lords ride in through the snow to pay their respects, and to take the measure of the new head of the house.
column18: {=ARM_KR_039_1a_Q}How will you honour the dead lord?

column15: {=ARM_KR_039_2_U}Ravens bring word that {DEAD} has died of old age. As is the custom of the river lords, the body is laid in a small boat and pushed out onto the current at dusk, and the heir looses a burning arrow after it as it drifts away.
column16: {=ARM_KR_039_2_L}{HEIR} now leads {HOUSE}. Lords and knights of the Trident ride in to pay their respects, and to take the measure of the new head of the house.
column18: {=ARM_KR_039_2_Q}How will you honour the dead lord?

column15: {=ARM_KR_039_3_U}Ravens bring word that {DEAD} has died of old age, in bed and not in battle, which the ironborn count a poor death. A drowned priest in sealskin carries the body out into the cold surf while the captains chant the old words of the Drowned God.
column16: {=ARM_KR_039_3_L}{HEIR} now leads {HOUSE}. Captains come from every island to drink to the dead, and to take the measure of the new head of the house.
column18: {=ARM_KR_039_3_Q}How will you honour the dead lord?

column15: {=ARM_KR_040_1_U}Before the yellow walls of Yunkai, two sellsword companies stand against the dragon queen. In the night a swaggering captain with a forked blue beard, Daario Naharis, comes to her tent with the heads of his fellow captains and lays his company's banners at her feet.
column16: {=ARM_KR_040_1_L}Her Unsullied fall on the other sellswords before dawn. The Second Sons, battered and leaderless, choose a new captain and turn their cloaks as well. Yunkai yields without a siege, and the sellswords of the bay remember whom they serve.

column15: {=ARM_KR_040_1a_U}Before the yellow walls of Yunkai, sellsword companies stand against the dragon queen, but gold and fear work faster than steel. One captain after another comes to her tent by night and lays his banners at her feet.
column16: {=ARM_KR_040_1a_L}The Second Sons, battered in a night attack by the Unsullied, choose a new captain and turn their cloaks. Yunkai yields without a siege, and the sellswords of the bay remember whom they serve.

column15: {=ARM_KR_041_1_U}Davos Seaworth survived the burning river clinging to a rock in the bay, only to be thrown into the dungeons of Dragonstone for threatening the red woman. Above him Melisandre sets three leeches on a frightened boy, a bastard of King Robert, and gives them full of royal blood to Stannis.
column16: {=ARM_KR_041_1_L}Stannis throws them one by one into the brazier and names the usurpers as he does: Robb Stark, Balon Greyjoy, Joffrey Baratheon. Those who hear it are sure it is only a mummer's show. The red woman is not.

column15: {=ARM_KR_041_1a_U}Davos Seaworth survived the burning river clinging to a rock in the bay, only to be thrown into the dungeons of Dragonstone for threatening the red woman. Above him Melisandre sets three leeches on a frightened boy, a bastard of King Robert, and gives them full of royal blood to Stannis.
column16: {=ARM_KR_041_1a_L}Stannis throws them one by one into the brazier and names the false kings who stand between him and the throne. Those who hear it call it a mummer's show, yet some of those names have already begun to fall.

column15: {=ARM_KR_041_2_U}Stannis names Davos his Hand, against all counsel. Davos learns that Melisandre wants the bastard boy burned to wake stone dragons, and on a dark night he rows the child out of Dragonstone to a Lysene ship bound across the narrow sea.
column16: {=ARM_KR_041_2_L}Stannis is furious, but Davos brings him something else: a letter from the Night's Watch, begging the kings of Westeros for help against what comes from beyond the Wall. Stannis reads it twice, and then calls for Melisandre.

column15: {=ARM_KR_042_1_U}A storm howls over Pyke, and old King Balon Greyjoy crosses the swaying rope bridge to the Sea Tower as he has done a thousand times. In the morning his broken body washes up on the rocks below. The ironborn whisper that the bridge was cut, or that the Drowned God called him home.
column16: {=ARM_KR_042_1_L}Within days a ship with red sails comes into the harbour. Euron Crow's Eye, the brother Balon exiled, walks into the castle and sits down on the Seastone Chair before anyone can stop him. The captains do not like it.

column15: {=ARM_KR_042_1a_U}A storm howls over Pyke, and old King Balon Greyjoy crosses the swaying rope bridge to the Sea Tower as he has done a thousand times. In the morning his broken body washes up on the rocks below. The ironborn whisper that the bridge was cut, or that the Drowned God called him home.
column16: {=ARM_KR_042_1a_L}With Euron Crow's Eye dead, Victarion, Lord Captain of the Iron Fleet, sails home and takes the Seastone Chair by right of strength. The islands accept him, for now.

column15: {=ARM_KR_042_1b_U}A storm howls over Pyke, and old King Balon Greyjoy crosses the swaying rope bridge to the Sea Tower as he has done a thousand times. In the morning his broken body washes up on the rocks below. The ironborn whisper that the bridge was cut, or that the Drowned God called him home.
column16: {=ARM_KR_042_1b_L}Neither of his brothers is left alive to claim the Seastone Chair. His daughter Yara takes her father's seat, and the captains who sneer at a woman's rule find her sharper than their axes.

column15: {=ARM_KR_042_2_U}The priest Aeron Damphair calls a kingsmoot, the first in centuries. Beneath the great stone ribs of Nagga on Old Wyk the captains gather and argue. Victarion offers strength, Yara offers peace and farms on the stony shore. Then Euron speaks, and offers them a horn that binds dragons.
column16: {=ARM_KR_042_2_L}He promises the captains all of Westeros, won with fire and sea. They roar his name and raise him on their shoulders, while Aeron's drowned men mutter that a godless man now wears the driftwood crown.
column18: {=ARM_KR_042_2_Q}The captains call on every ironborn lord. Whose name do you shout?

column15: {=ARM_KR_043_1_U}King Robb has no child of his own, and he believes his younger brothers lost. Before he marches to the Twins he gathers his lords in a candlelit chamber at Riverrun and dictates his will. In it he legitimizes his bastard brother Jon Snow and names him heir to the North.
column16: {=ARM_KR_043_1_L}Some of the older lords argue, but one after another they press their seals into the wax. If the king falls, the North will know whom to follow, even if Jon has sworn himself to the Wall.
column18: {=ARM_KR_043_1_Q}The king's lords press their seals to the will. Will you add yours?

column15: {=ARM_KR_044_1_U}The Hound has dragged Arya Stark across the Riverlands to sell her back to her family at the Twins, where her uncle Edmure is to be married. They arrive in the rain to the sound of music. Then the music changes, and the camp outside the castle turns into a slaughter.
column16: {=ARM_KR_044_1_L}Arya tries to run toward the gate to find her mother and brother. Sandor knocks her senseless with the flat of his axe and carries her off into the night. Behind them the Freys are killing the northmen in their tents.

column15: {=ARM_KR_044_2_U}At the inn on the crossroads, Arya and the Hound find Polliver and the Tickler drinking with their men, and Polliver wears Arya's stolen sword Needle at his belt. Words turn to steel. When it is over the Lannister men lie dead on the floor and Needle is back in Arya's hand.
column16: {=ARM_KR_044_2_L}But the Hound is badly hurt and the wound turns foul. Arya leaves him dying under a tree by the Trident and rides to Saltpans, where an iron coin buys her passage on a ship to Braavos.

column15: {=ARM_KR_044_2a_U}At the inn on the crossroads, Arya and the Hound find Lannister soldiers drinking, and one of them wears Arya's stolen sword Needle at his belt. Words turn to steel. When it is over the soldiers lie dead on the floor and Needle is back in Arya's hand.
column16: {=ARM_KR_044_2a_L}But the Hound is badly hurt and the wound turns foul. Arya leaves him dying under a tree by the Trident and rides to Saltpans, where an iron coin buys her passage on a ship to Braavos.

column15: {=ARM_KR_044_3_U}Outlaws fall on the little port of Saltpans by night. Their leader wears the Hound's great dog helm, and the smallfolk who survive swear the Hound himself has come back as a monster. The holdfast is stormed, the boats are burned and many townsfolk are cut down in the streets.
column16: {=ARM_KR_044_3_L}Saltpans will be a long time recovering. The raiders have taken to the hills along the coast, and the lords of the Riverlands offer a reward to anyone who brings back the dog helm and the man wearing it.

column15: {=ARM_KR_045_1_U}The war has passed over the villages around {PLACE} more than once. Those who lost their homes, their harvest and their families have stopped waiting for a lord to save them. Deserters and burned out farmers have gone into the woods together, and they no longer ask for what they take.
column16: {=ARM_KR_045_1_L}In the inns men speak of a new band and of the nickname of the man who leads it. The captains of the guard are posting notices. Many of the outlaws were good men once, before the war broke them.

column15: {=ARM_KR_046_1_U}On the road to Meereen the Great Masters nailed a slave child to every milepost, each one pointing toward the city. Daenerys counts them all. Her freedmen open the gates in the night, and when the great pyramid falls she orders the same number of masters nailed up in the plaza.
column16: {=ARM_KR_046_1_L}Some of those masters had spoken against the deed. Her councillors whisper that justice and vengeance look alike from a distance, and Meereen watches its new queen in fear. How she rules now will decide whether the city ever loves her.
column18: {=ARM_KR_046_1_Q}The queen asks her counsellors what should be done. What do you say?

column15: {=ARM_KR_046_2_U}The old squire Arstan Whitebeard kneels before Daenerys and confesses that he is Ser Barristan Selmy, once Lord Commander of King Robert's Kingsguard. He also reveals what he knew at court: in her first months in Essos, Ser Jorah Mormont sold reports of her to the Spider.
column16: {=ARM_KR_046_2_L}Jorah does not deny it. Daenerys cannot bear to see him die, nor to see him near her, and she sends him from her side. Ser Barristan takes his place as her first sword, and the queen stays in Meereen to learn how to rule.

column15: {=ARM_KR_047_1_U}Days after the wedding at the Twins, outlaws of the Brotherhood pull a woman's body from the Green Fork. Her throat is cut to the bone and her hair has gone white. Lord Beric bends over her and gives her the fiery kiss of the red god, and Catelyn Stark opens her eyes.
column16: {=ARM_KR_047_1_L}She cannot speak above a croak and she cannot forgive. Since that night the Brotherhood hangs every Frey it can catch, and the smallfolk whisper of a grey lady in a hood who sits in judgment at the outlaws' fires.

column15: {=ARM_KR_047_2_U}Searching the Riverlands for Sansa Stark, Brienne of Tarth is taken by the Brotherhood and brought before their hooded lady. Brienne carries a sword with a golden lion on its hilt, a gift of the Kingslayer, and the lady hears no excuses: she must bring Jaime Lannister to them, or hang.
column16: {=ARM_KR_047_2_L}With the rope already around her neck, Brienne cries out a single word. Days later she finds Jaime at a village by the Trident and begs him to come with her, without saying where. Then she is gone from the roads for a while.

column15: {=ARM_KR_048_1_U}Mance Rayder sends a war band of Thenns, clansmen in bronze armour, to climb the Wall far from any castle, and Jon Snow, still playing the turncloak, climbs the ice beside them. South of the Wall they raid and kill, and Jon must play along to stay alive.
column16: {=ARM_KR_048_1_L}At the first chance Jon breaks away, takes an arrow in the leg and rides for Castle Black to warn his brothers. Behind him the Thenns are loose in the Gift, burning villages on their way south.

column15: {=ARM_KR_048_2_U}The Thenns burn Mole's Town and fall on Castle Black from the south, where it has no wall. Old men, green boys and a limping Jon Snow hold the stairs and the king's tower through the night with arrows, fire and spears.
column16: {=ARM_KR_048_2_L}At dawn the attack breaks. Among the dead lies a red haired spearwife with an arrow in her chest, and Jon holds her as she dies. The Watch has no time to mourn, for the great host of Mance Rayder is already marching south.

column15: {=ARM_KR_048_2a_U}The Thenns burn Mole's Town and fall on Castle Black from the south, where it has no wall. Old men, green boys and a limping Jon Snow hold the stairs and the king's tower through the night with arrows, fire and spears.
column16: {=ARM_KR_048_2a_L}At dawn the attack breaks and the raiders who still live flee into the woods. The Watch has no time to mourn its dead, for the great host of Mance Rayder is already marching south.
